paraphrase: Kālī, ever full of bliss, enchantress of Mahākāla: you dance by yourself, sing by yourself and clap your own hands in time — the world is the Mother's own play.
notes: Attributed to Kamalākānta in the Ramakrishna literature; attribution not checked.
speaker: Kamalākānta
translation_basis: the song as commonly sung in Bengal; wording and attribution vary

location.section: song 'Śyāmā mā ki āmār kālo re'

paraphrase: Is my Mother Śyāmā black? People call Kālī black, but my heart does not: the black-formed, sky-clad one lights up the lotus of the heart; she is sometimes white, sometimes yellow, blue or red — the singer cannot say what she is.
notes: Usually attributed to Kamalākānta, sometimes to Rāmprasād.
speaker: Kamalākānta
translation_basis: the song as commonly sung in Bengal; wording and attribution vary
